newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippine oil firms seek early settlement of dues.
newsitem.headline: Philippine oil firms seek early settlement of dues.

text.p: The Philippine government should settle the dues of the country's three petroleum firms or it could affect the country's oil sector deregulation programme, industry officials said on Thursday.
"It may not be legal for the government to push through with full deregulation in March next year without payment of the claims," a top official of Caltex Philippines told Reuters.

Caltex, a unit of Caltex Petroleum Corp, is one of the three firms awaiting from the government payments totalling 2.4 billion pesos ($92 million) as dues from the Oil Price Stabilisation Fund (OPSF).
"We are hard pressed for liquidity and as much as possible we want our money right now," the official, who did not want to be named, told Reuters.
The OPSF is a buffer fund that is a relic from the days when the country's oil sector was under complete state control.

Oil prices were fixed by the government and the OPSF was meant to help soften the impact of fluctuations in international crude prices. The oil firms' claims on the OPSF grew larger as international prices kept rising.
This year the government started deregulating the oil industry in phases and oil prices are meant to be completely freed by March next year after which the OPSF is to be abolished.
On Tuesday, the government said it would pay the oil firms their dues by sourcing funds from the 1998 budgetary allocations.

"It is only fair and equitable that the oil industry which has already waited for an inordinate amount of time should be allowed to recover the claims. Necessary funding should be appropriated and made immediately available," Oscar Reyes, Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp vice-president for finance said.
Pilipinas Shell is a unit of the Royal Dutch/Shell Group.
Petron Corp sources said they hoped the government would settle the claims soon.
